newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Supply rises on Bulgaria depo mkt after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Supply rises on Bulgaria depo mkt after rate hike.

text.p: Demand remained high on Bulgaria's interbank deposit market, but supply picked up from recent lows after the central bank (BNB) imposed a package of lev-boosting measures, traders said.
"Supply rose after the new interest rate of 300 percent went in force, and some tough monetary restrictions were loosened," a commercial bank dealer said.
Dealers said BNB's measures were likely to relieve liquidity pressure on cash-strapped banks and boost money market activity.
The BNB on Monday raised its central interest rate (CIR) to an all-time high of 300 percent from 108 percent to counter high inflation expectations amid an economic crisis.
In a bid to normalise settlement and restore confidence among commercial banks the BNB also said it would support banks with liquidity problems through its open market operations.
In addition, the central bank said it would allow banks to use up to a half of their minimum required reserves for emergency refinancing each month.
Currently, banks were allowed to use only 10 percent of minimum reserves for such refinancing.
"Central bank decisions will probably further boost supply of lev funds on the deposit market," another dealer said.
The premium on banks' overnight deposits' rate fell to 2.0-3.0 points over the current CIR from 6.0-8.0 points above the previous CIR on Monday.

The rate on one-week collateralised deposits retreated to 4-4.5 points over the CIR from 10 points over CIR and two-week deposit rate fell to 7.0-8.0 points from 16-20 on Monday. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
